The BL19 digital collection retrieval benchmark is described in Cultural Analytics for Good: Building Inclusive Evaluation Frameworks for Historical IR [1]. It uses the British Library BL19 digital collection of more than 35,000 works from 1700–1899 to study retrieval and language change in 19th-century fiction and non-fiction [1].

The benchmark is built with expert-driven query design, paragraph-level relevance annotation, and LLM assistance to create a scalable evaluation framework grounded in human expertise [1]. It specifically studies knowledge transfer from fiction to non-fiction, asking how narrative understanding and semantic richness in fiction can improve retrieval for scholarly and factual materials [1].
